modernGeography.modernRelationshipNote: Located on the right bank of the Indus River in modern Larkana District, Sindh, Pakistan.

shortDescription: One of the most extensively excavated metropolises of the ancient world, featuring a fortified citadel, multi-storey brick houses, covered drains, and the bitumen-sealed Great Bath.

sources.title: Mohenjo-daro and the Indus Civilization
sources.note: Initial comprehensive excavation reports detailing the Great Bath and street grid.

connections.label: Inspect the 3D model of the Great Bath

modernGeography.modernRelationshipNote: Situated near an ancient course of the Ravi River in modern Sahiwal District, Punjab, Pakistan.

shortDescription: The first discovered settlement of the Indus civilization, characterized by massive circular working floors, brick workshops, and a large granary complex.

sources.title: Excavations at Harappa
sources.authorOrCitation: Vats, Madho Sarup (1940), Government of India Press

connections.label: Northern urban anchor of the civilization

modernGeography.modernRelationshipNote: Situated near the Gulf of Khambhat in modern Ahmedabad District, Gujarat, India.

shortDescription: A premier maritime trading port equipped with a massive brick tidal basin (interpreted as a dockyard) and bead-making workshops exporting carnelian to Mesopotamia.

modernGeography.modernRelationshipNote: Occupies the riverfront confluence of the Ganga and Son rivers, directly under modern Patna, Bihar.

shortDescription: Described by Greek envoy Megasthenes as a grand timber-fortified metropolis spanning nine miles along the Ganga, serving successively as the supreme capital for the Mauryan and Gupta empires.

sources.title: Indika
sources.note: Eye-witness Hellenistic description of Pataliputra's moat, wooden palisades, and royal courts.

historicalRole: Site of the Lion Capital & Ashoka Pillar

modernGeography.modernRelationshipNote: Located roughly 10 kilometres north-east of Varanasi in eastern Uttar Pradesh, India.

shortDescription: The sacred deer park where the Buddha delivered his first discourse, and where Emperor Ashoka erected the polished Chunar sandstone pillar crowned with four back-to-back lions.

sources.title: Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum: Inscriptions of Asoka
sources.authorOrCitation: Hultzsch, E. (1925), Archaeological Survey of India

connections.label: View the Sarnath Lion Capital exhibit

modernGeography.modernRelationshipNote: Situated near modern Rajgir and Bihar Sharif in Nalanda District, Bihar, India.

shortDescription: One of antiquity's greatest residential monasteries, housing up to ten thousand students and two thousand teachers studying philosophy, medicine, logic, and astronomy.

sources.title: Buddhist Records of the Western World
sources.note: Detailed seventh-century travelogue documenting curriculum, admission debates, and nine-storey libraries.

historicalRole: Mughal River Capital & Site of the Taj Mahal

modernGeography.modernRelationshipNote: Situated on the banks of the Yamuna River in western Uttar Pradesh, India.

shortDescription: The primary administrative and court capital of the high Mughal empire, transformed by riverfront garden-palaces culminating in the Taj Mahal commissioned by Shah Jahan in 1632.

sources.title: The Complete Taj Mahal and the Riverfront Gardens of Agra
sources.note: Authoritative architectural monograph on the Yamuna riverfront garden city and Taj Mahal complex.

connections.label: Explore the 3D model of the Taj Mahal

modernGeography.modernRelationshipNote: Directly comprises Old Delhi (including Chandni Chowk and the Red Fort) within the National Capital Territory of Delhi, India.
modernGeography.modernEquivalentName: Old Delhi, NCT of Delhi, India

shortDescription: The planned walled city founded by Shah Jahan in 1639, centered upon the colossal red sandstone palace-fortress (Lal Qila) and the central boulevard of Chandni Chowk.

sources.title: Shahjahanabad: The Sovereign City in Mughal India
sources.authorOrCitation: Blake, Stephen P. (1991), Cambridge University Press

connections.label: Explore the 3D model of the Red Fort

modernGeography.modernRelationshipNote: A coastal village along the Arabian Sea in modern Navsari District, Gujarat, India.

shortDescription: The coastal destination of the 390-kilometre trek from Sabarmati Ashram, where Mahatma Gandhi lifted natural salt on 6 April 1930, defying the British salt tax and launching the Civil Disobedience Movement.

sources.title: The Salt March: The Groundwork for Indian Independence

connections.label: Read exhibit details on the Salt March

modernGeography.modernRelationshipNote: A barrier island separating Pulicat Lake from the Bay of Bengal in Tirupati District, Andhra Pradesh, India.

shortDescription: India's spaceport on the Bay of Bengal from which the LVM3 rocket carrying Chandrayaan-3 launched on 14 July 2023, culminating in the historic Vikram landing at the lunar south pole.
